headline: Armless Racing Driver Breaks Barriers at 110 mph, Eyes Le Mans
meta_description: 23-year-old Callum Smith steers with his feet and just signed with Team BRIT, racing toward a historic place at Le Mans 24 Hours.
summary_short: Born without arms, Callum Smith has clocked 110 mph on track and signed with Team BRIT—the world's only all-disabled racing team.
body:
At 23, Callum Smith is rewriting what's possible in motorsport. Born without arms, he has already steered a race car to speeds exceeding 110 mph, and he's now chasing a seat at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, one of motorsport's most demanding events. This summer, Smith signed his first driver contract with Team BRIT, the world's only competitive racing team made up entirely of disabled drivers. His goal is historic: to become the first armless driver ever to race at that level.

Smith's love affair with racing began early. Watching bike racing with his grandfather at age two planted the seed, but his dream took shape when he sent a bold email to Team BRIT expressing his interest. They responded, he passed their tests, and by July 2025 he completed his first track day, hitting 90 mph at Donington Park. Four months later, he clocked 100 mph on the Silverstone Formula One circuit in his own Audi A3. Now he's training in Team BRIT's modified BMW 1 Series, mastering a custom setup where his left foot operates the steering plate and his right foot controls the accelerator and brake.

The work is demanding. "It's hard, there's a lot of eye to foot coordination," Smith said, noting that race car steering feels heavier than he expected. Yet his daily life already demonstrates his adaptability—he writes with his right foot, plays Xbox, and performs guitar with his feet. That same determination drives him forward. "I'm going to be the first person to be racing without any arms, the first one ever," he said. With his racing license still in progress, Smith is putting in the work to make that statement reality.
quick_facts: 23-year-old born without arms; steers with feet only
Signed first contract with Team BRIT, all-disabled racing team
Hit 110 mph on track; training in modified BMW 1 Series
Aiming for 24 Hours of Le Mans competition
